claims.explanation: Saracatinib is a SRC-family kinase inhibitor, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on SRC/YES1 signaling, which is often driven by epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) activation. Lines with mesenchymal-like phenotypes, EGFR mutations, or PIK3CA mutations may be more sensitive, while PTEN loss and BRAF mutations may confer resistance. The virtual cell data showing similarity to SRC inhibitors supports this mechanism.

features.basis: SRC is the primary target of saracatinib; high expression may indicate dependence
YES1 is a target of saracatinib; high expression may increase sensitivity
EGFR mutations are enriched in sensitive lines and may activate SRC signaling
PIK3CA mutations are common in sensitive lines and may cooperate with SRC inhibition
PTEN loss is enriched in resistant lines and may activate PI3K/AKT bypass signaling
BRAF mutations are common in resistant melanoma lines and may drive MAPK-mediated resistance
E-cadherin restoration by saracatinib suggests epithelial lines may be less sensitive
Intermediate mesenchymal phenotype with high ZEB1 is sensitive to saracatinib
NF1 mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may activate RAS/RTK signaling
TP53 mutations are frequent in sensitive lines but also common in resistant lines, weak evidence
KRAS mutations appear in some resistant lines and may drive MAPK-mediated resistance
ABL1 is a target of saracatinib; high expression may increase sensitivity
